P07|A.how: In form A sparing a neighbour takes conditions: it rests on overlapping membership, valued neighbouring art or fear of retaliation, and it depends on placers whom the negotiators admit they cannot control.

P08|A.how: In form A border terms take work and meet limits: members prepare a deal inside the room, check the counterpart and cede background pixels before picture pixels, and members find that identity colours limit what they concede and that uncontrolled placers can defeat a promise.

A05|A.how: In form A a settled border is kept only in part: restraint often comes before any settlement is shown, and a treaty guides the members who learn and accept it while others keep placing against it.

A14|A.how: In form A help is part of the bargain more than its result: pixels and shared upkeep are offered as the terms, or help is already under way when the bargaining starts, so help delivered after a settled border is not shown.

P07|B.how: In form B sparing passes through the room's tools: an instruction to spare agreed space must reach script users as a target update, a requested template carries a restoration attempt, and admitted script damage brings apology and repair without an attack call.

P08|B.how: In form B border talk has steps before and after it: members ask for a treaty before any damage, seek local consensus before a proposal, tell organized allies from hostile placers, and relay a negotiated move to builders by private message and announcement.

A05|B.how: In form B a settled border is kept where its terms reach the placers: restraint follows where placers learned of the agreement and where script targets were updated, and a memorial is spared with no border settled.

P07|C.how: In form C restraint is linked to a reason the room states: an apology after a complaint, help or space received from the neighbour, or the room's own identity given as the reason not to attack.

P08|C.how: In form C agreements are kept apart from compliance: members report attacks after announced terms, visitors admit limits on controlling placers, and a truce needs a counterpart able to keep its terms.

P16|C.how: In form C help is part of the room's own building: helpers alternate placements between the two works, paired scripts give spare capacity to the neighbour, and requests and offers stay apart from delivered help.

A13|C.how: In form C help between rooms does not follow a shortage of hands: donors help from completed or well-kept work, help comes with construction and overlap repair, and a proposal for outside help is not shown to bring the later offer.

P07|D.how: In form D restraint has conditions of its own: it protects the room's own logo, repays prior help, and does not reach every placer, since one member's promise cannot bind another placer who uses many accounts.

P16|D.how: In form D help waits on the helper's own work: donors give when their work is secure and pixels are spare, may refuse a request that brings a dispute with it, and see that help in one relationship can remove a third room's mark.

P19|D.how: In form D hosting shows as requests and expectations: guests ask for space or depend on a host, but a grant, an approval procedure or a durable host rule is not shown.

A05|D.how: In form D a settled border is kept where the agreement reaches a receptive placer, since some placers do not learn of the truce, and some members spare neighbours by a norm against damaging art with no treaty.

A13|D.how: In form D help between rooms comes from surplus more than shortage: donors give after their own work is finished or safe, repay earlier protection, and put off help while their home defence is short.

A10|E.how: In form E judging the hands too few ends one member's part or one expansion, not the room's place: the others keep repairing, recruit or finish, and no completed move is shown to follow.

A16|E.how: In form E restraint answers reported harm, overlap or a contemplated enlargement, not a written attack call refused inside the room.

P19|F.how: In form F hosting shows only at the request stage: a room applies, or asks a larger mark for shelter, and a grant, protection or residence under host rules is not shown.

P27|F.how: In form F the choice of spot also comes after a loss: the room picks a new site or a backup while another of its works has been lost, so the before-loss bound holds for the site decision, not for the room's whole history.

A04|F.how: In form F border talk comes before keeping: rooms ask neighbours for permission or access while they look for a spot or build, before any stable mark exists to keep.

A10|F.how: In form F the move answers the spot more than the hands: a taken spot or a lack of permitted space moves the room, and where too few hands are named, the move is proposed or hesitant rather than shown to follow.
